enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity. You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **f)** What are some of the negative effects of drugs on students and the society at large?
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: define drugs and drug abuse among young people in Cameroon.
2. Effects on students: poor health, poor results, drop-out, bad company.
3. Effects on society: crime, violence, broken families, cost to the nation.
4. A short example to illustrate.
5. Conclusion: what students, parents and the government should do.

**Model composition (470 words)**

Drugs are substances that change the way the body and the mind work. Some, like medicines, are useful when a doctor prescribes them. Others, such as cannabis, tramadol, cocaine and cheap alcohol, are taken for pleasure and are very dangerous. In many Cameroonian towns, these substances are sold near schools and motor parks, and many young people have started to use them. The effects on students and on the society at large are serious.

First, drugs destroy the health of the student. A boy who smokes cannabis may start to cough, lose his appetite and become thin and weak. Strong drugs attack the brain and the liver and can cause madness or even sudden death. Because the body of an adolescent is still growing, the damage is greater than in an adult.

Second, drugs ruin the studies of those who take them. A student under the influence cannot concentrate in class, forgets what the teacher has said and often sleeps at his desk. He starts to miss lessons and to refuse homework. His marks fall, he repeats classes, and in the end he may leave school altogether. Parents who have spent their savings on school fees are left with nothing but regret. In addition, a user needs money to buy drugs, so he may lie to his parents, sell his books or steal from other pupils.

Third, drug abuse harms the society as a whole. Young people who are addicted often join gangs and commit crimes such as armed robbery, rape and fights. In several towns, residents are afraid to walk at night because of such groups. Families are also broken, since a drug addict may beat his parents, insult his neighbours and bring shame to his house. Meanwhile, the government spends large sums of money on police, hospitals and prisons that could be used to build schools and roads. A nation whose youths are drugged loses the energy and talent it needs to grow.

I remember a classmate called Ngu who was the best pupil in our class in Form Three. After he met some older boys in the quarter, he began to smoke secretly. Within a year, his eyes were red, his marks had collapsed and he was caught stealing a phone. Today he lives on the streets, and his mother cries whenever she hears his name.

What can be done? Parents should watch their children closely and talk to them openly. Teachers should organise clubs and lectures to warn pupils about drugs. The government should punish those who sell drugs and should open rehabilitation centres for those who are addicted. Above all, students must learn to say a firm "no" to bad friends.

In conclusion, drugs bring sickness, failure and crime. If we protect our young people today, we shall secure a healthy and prosperous society tomorrow.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Effects on BOTH students and the society, each developed with explanation or example, with a conclusion giving solutions |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, a style and tone suited to the topic, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Writing only about students (or only about the society) and ignoring the other part of the question.
2. Listing effects in one-line sentences with no explanation or example.
